takeaway: The sciatic nerve supplies the posterior thigh: biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus and the ischial part of adductor magnus.

question.text: A 25-year-old woman fractures her pelvis in a road traffic accident, and her sciatic nerve is thought to be injured as it exits the pelvis. Which muscle will lose its innervation?
question.say: A twenty-five-year-old woman fractures her pelvis in a road traffic accident, and her sciatic nerve is thought to be injured as it exits the pelvis. Which muscle will lose its innervation?

lines.text: Her pelvic fracture has injured the sciatic nerve as it leaves the pelvis.
It is the largest nerve in the body, and it divides at the popliteal fossa into tibial and common peroneal nerves.
In general, it supplies the posterior compartment of the thigh: the hamstrings.
Biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus all switch off.
Semimembranosus is the only one among the options, so it loses its supply.
Sartorius and the adductors have other nerves, so they stay lit.
